expectation: Membrane/cytoplasmic rings on monocytes and macrophages, which are common in a tumour. They should be scattered or clustered in the stroma and at the tumour–stroma interface, and largely absent from tumour cell nests. Expect a moderate fraction of cells to be positive.
observed: A: stromal, network-like yellow in most tiles, with dark nest-shaped regions left unstained; one tile has dense patchy aggregates. B: scattered cells with membrane signal in stroma. C: mostly dim (likely a tumour nest). D: clear rings around nuclei.
why: Ring-shaped staining is confined to stromal and myeloid-rich regions and spares tumour nests, which fits a monocyte/macrophage marker.
notes: CD14 follows stromal and myeloid-rich areas and spares the nest-like regions. The close-up shows membrane rings around nuclei. Background is high in some tiles, but the pattern is cell-specific rather than haze.
